Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that the experts' recommendations for follow-up care after new cardiovascular implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) were not consistently implemented in routine clinical practice.

While some studies suggest that initial follow-up visits were improved over time and more common among white patients compared to other races, there was no mention of whether these recommendations are still followed by healthcare professionals in general practice settings.

In fact, the majority of the retrieved matches provide information on alternative approaches or considerations for following up with patients after implantable devices, such as the importance of considering additional areas of investigation (Prompt 7) or the need to improve adherence to follow-up procedures (Prompts 23 and 47).

Therefore, based on this analysis, it is unlikely that experts' recommendations for routine clinical practice are being followed consistently.
